sections.h2: How do you sell a house in Atlanta, Georgia?
sections.html:
Atlanta homeowners can list through an agent, sell without one, or take a cash offer for the house as it stands. Because the city crosses two counties and holds more than 240 distinct neighborhoods, the right route depends heavily on the block, the condition of the house and the tax office that bills it.

Atlanta began in 1837 as the end point of a state-sponsored railroad, took the name Marthasville in 1843, and became the City of Atlanta on December 29, 1847. It is the county seat of Fulton County and extends into DeKalb County, covers about 135 square miles of land, and sits at roughly 1,050 feet above sea level.

  • Agent listing: strongest for houses in neighborhoods with steady sales and buyers who expect staging.
  • Owner sale: possible when you can price your own house from comparable sales and manage the closing attorney yourself.
  • Cash as-is sale: common for inherited homes, tired rentals, houses with code or repair problems, and owners facing a deadline.

sections.h2: What do Census numbers say about Atlanta housing?
sections.html:
Atlanta grew faster than Albany, Alpharetta or Athens-Clarke County. The Census Bureau estimates 529,110 residents as of July 1, 2025, which is 6.1 percent above the April 2020 base of 498,805, and the 2020 density was 3,685.7 people per square mile.

sections.h2: How do Atlanta's neighborhoods differ for a seller?
sections.html:
Atlanta has three high-rise districts that run north to south along Peachtree Street and Peachtree Road: Downtown, Midtown and Buckhead. Downtown has the most office space in the metro area, Midtown is the second-largest business district and a center for arts and higher education, and Buckhead, about eight miles north of Downtown, is the third-largest business district.

Around those districts are low- and medium-density neighborhoods where the craftsman bungalow is the dominant single-family house. The eastside includes historic streetcar suburbs built between the 1890s and the 1930s, such as Inman Park, with its Victorian houses. Emory University was annexed into the city effective January 1, 2018. A seller should describe the house by its neighborhood name, because buyers search that way and the city recognizes 242 officially defined neighborhoods.

sections.h2: Who sets the property tax on an Atlanta house, Fulton County or DeKalb County?
sections.html:
It depends on which side of the county line the parcel lies. Most of Atlanta is in Fulton County, where the Board of Assessors issues a notice every year and the owner can appeal within 45 days of the date on that notice. The part of Atlanta in DeKalb County is assessed by DeKalb County, so a DeKalb-side seller should ask that county's assessors for the appeal date and procedure on their own notice.

  • In Fulton County, only the assessed value can be appealed, and the deadline printed on the notice controls.
  • Appeals can be filed online, by mail, or in person, including at the Board of Assessors office at 141 Pryor Street, Suite 1018.
  • Fulton filers choose a Board of Equalization hearing, non-binding arbitration or a Hearing Officer, and a temporary tax bill may arrive while the appeal is pending.

If you are mid-appeal when you sell, tell the closing attorney so the settlement statement can reflect any temporary tax bill.

sections.h2: Do short-term rental rules affect an Atlanta house sale?
sections.html:
They can. The Atlanta City Council adopted its short-term rental ordinance, 20-0-1656, on March 15, 2021, and the rules took effect on March 1, 2022. The ordinance allows an owner or long-term tenant to license a primary residence and one additional dwelling unit, and hosts must post the city license number on every advertisement.

The Department of City Planning handles appeals of license decisions, and hosts apply through the city's online permitting portal at any time. Questions go to the city's short-term rental email address, STR@atlantaga.gov. If your house is marketed to buyers as a nightly rental, check the license status first and give the buyer a clear answer on whether the license can move to a new owner.

The city notes that its enforcement date has been extended and that implementation may change, so ask the Department of City Planning what applies to your parcel before you describe the house as a rental.

sections.h2: How do Atlanta's trees, rain and traffic affect house showings?
sections.html:
Atlanta has a humid subtropical climate, with hot, humid summers, mild but variable winters and about 50 inches of rain a year spread through the seasons. The city is often called the City in a Forest because it has the densest urban tree cover of any major city in the United States, so tree health, roof and gutter condition and drainage around the foundation matter to inspectors.

Interstates 20, 75 and 85 meet here, and I-75 and I-85 combine as the Downtown Connector, which carries more than 340,000 vehicles per day. I-285, known as the Perimeter, separates Inside the Perimeter from Outside the Perimeter, a distinction that buyers use when they search. MARTA runs buses, heavy rail and a downtown light rail loop, and the Atlanta Streetcar covers a 2.7 mile Downtown Loop.

sections.h2: What Georgia transfer rules apply when an Atlanta house sells?
sections.html:
Georgia's real estate transfer tax must be paid before the deed can be recorded with the Clerk of Superior Court. The Department of Revenue states the rate as $1 for the first $1,000 or fractional part, and 10 cents for each additional $100 or fractional part, with the seller liable unless the contract says otherwise.

The GSCCCA runs the electronic PT-61 filing that accompanies the deed, and the Georgia Department of Revenue refers questions about exemptions to the Clerk of Superior Court. For an Atlanta property, that is the clerk of Fulton County or DeKalb County, depending on where the parcel sits.

faqs.q: Which county handles my Atlanta property tax appeal?
faqs.a: It depends on the parcel. Fulton County handles the Fulton portion of Atlanta, with a 45-day appeal window from the notice date, and DeKalb County handles the DeKalb portion.

faqs.q: Do I need a license to rent my Atlanta house nightly?
faqs.a: Yes. Atlanta's ordinance requires a short-term rental license, and hosts must post the license on every advertisement. Apply through the city's online permitting portal.

faqs.q: What is the median home value in Atlanta?
faqs.a: The Census Bureau puts the median value of owner-occupied homes in Atlanta at $439,600 for 2020-2024. Your own house may differ widely by neighborhood.

faqs.q: Who pays Georgia's transfer tax on an Atlanta sale?
faqs.a: The seller is liable, although the sales contract can shift the cost to the buyer. The state rate is $1 for the first $1,000 plus 10 cents per additional $100.

faqs.q: Can I sell my Atlanta house with tenants living in it?
faqs.a: Yes. A tenant-occupied house can be sold with the lease in place. Read the lease for notice and entry terms, and give required notice before showings.
